The Classroom Problem

Built For The Reality Of Indian Higher Education.

Multilingual Code-Switching

Professors frequently switch between English, Hindi, and technical dialect in the middle of a sentence. Standard speech recognition engines fail or produce garbled text. Cereal is tuned for natural multilingual audio flow.

Automatic Deadline Extraction

Whenever a teacher says "Submit the assignment by next Tuesday 4 PM", Cereal isolates the due date, creates a task in Google Tasks, and blocks time on your Google Calendar automatically.

Foreground Audio Reliability

Phones lock, notifications arrive, and students switch between apps. Cereal utilizes a persistent foreground Android service to maintain high-bitrate AAC recording without system kills or interruptions.

Active Recall Generation

Automatically compiles dynamic multiple-choice quiz questions and flashcards directly from lecture content, allowing students to test themselves within minutes after the lecture finishes.

Zero-Cloud Telemetry Privacy

Raw audio stays strictly stored on your Android device. It is never sold, analyzed, or indexed by third-party tracking networks. You maintain complete control over your private recordings.

Battery-Conscious MediaCodec

Direct low-level Android MediaCodec hardware encoding uses less than 3% battery per hour of continuous recording, letting you capture an entire day of college classes without needing a charger.

Software Engineering

Native Kotlin & Jetpack Compose Pipeline

Built natively in Current Projects/Granola20/ (production package com.col.cereal), Cereal is engineered with modern Android Material 3, StateFlow, Room SQLite with FTS5 search, and Google OAuth2 (PKCE).

STAGE 01
Audio Capture Service
Hardware microphone input recorded to .m4a (AAC 44.1 kHz, 128 kbps) with battery-conscious low-memory buffers and foreground notification.
STAGE 02
Gemini 2.5 Flash
Audio payload streamed via HTTP to Google's sub-second multimodal model with zero hallucination prompt controls and markdown structure.
STAGE 03
Local SQLite Vault
Full-text searchable notes, audio checkpoints, and speaker metadata saved securely on-device with zero cloud lock-in.
STAGE 04
Calendar & Tasks Sync
REST API dispatcher converts identified action items into native Google Calendar events and Google Tasks with automatic time-blocking.

Yes. Cereal runs as a foreground Android service with a persistent system notification, holding an efficient CPU wake lock that ensures high-fidelity recording even when your phone is locked in your pocket.

Gemini 2.5 Flash is natively multimodal and pre-trained on diverse Indian linguistic patterns. It seamlessly decodes bilingual Hindi-English lecture delivery without producing phonetically confused transcripts.

Only two: microphone access for capture, and notification permission so Android can display the persistent recording service badge. No contacts, storage scanning, location, or background data harvesting is ever requested.

Recording and storage work fully offline — your audio is saved locally first with zero data loss. Only the synthesis step streams to Gemini, and pending lectures automatically upload for transcription the moment connectivity returns.

Because Cereal ships as a direct APK rather than a Play Store listing, Android flags any sideloaded package as "unknown publisher" by default. The build is signed, open-source, and auditable on GitHub — tap "Install Anyway" to proceed.

Cereal is 100% free and open-source. There are no subscriptions, ads, or artificial feature walls. You can supply your own free Google Gemini API key or use our studio's student quota.

A stock recorder hands you a raw audio file; Cereal hands you study material. It synthesizes searchable structured notes, extracts exam formulas, and dispatches dates and assignments straight into Google Calendar and Tasks — all in one tap.

Because Cereal uses efficient AAC-LC hardware compression at 128 kbps, a standard 60-minute lecture uses only ~57 MB of device storage.
